facts.fact: The implementers (MRCG at LSHTM, Ministry of Health, Shifo Foundation) state that from 1 October 2023 Bundung Maternal and Child Health Hospital's antenatal, delivery, postnatal and immunisation registers were replaced by scanned Smart Paper forms, with the monthly EPI and RMNCH indicators calculated from them and integrated into the matching DHIS2 datasets automatically, without manual reporting; one facility, a pilot.

The automatic monthly feed of indicators into DHIS2 is described at one site, Bundung Maternal and Child Health Hospital, which the paper calls an urban secondary-level public facility, from 1 October 2023; the paper does not say which other tiers enter DHIS2 data.

The paper states that the Ministry of Health generates the monthly reports and maps each indicator to its DHIS2 dataset, and that a Technical Working Group formed at the ministry, including its HMIS, planning, ICT and monitoring units, handled the integration with DHIS2 for the pilot that began in July 2023.

systems.country_label: Smart Paper Technology; electronic pregnancy registry
systems.platform: Smart Paper Technology (Shifo Foundation): scanned paper forms, MyShifo app, Clarity central repository
systems.owner: Ministry of Health with MRCG at LSHTM, Shifo Foundation and CDC
systems.tiers: immunisation: introduced 2016 at 4 fixed and 14 outreach points in the Western Regions, then scaled nationally to all EPI clinics; maternal and newborn: Bundung Maternal and Child Health Hospital (secondary level) from 1 October 2023, later extended there to all primary health care, replacing over 30 HMIS registers; Faji Kunda Major Health Centre from July 2024
central level receives monthly datasets; facility feed described at Bundung Maternal and Child Health Hospital only

note: Smart Paper Technology is classed tracker: patient-level records for immunisation and for maternal and newborn care, on a unique SPT ID. At Bundung alone the paper says it was extended to all primary health care and builds a medical history, which the parent may read as emr at one T2 hospital, scanned from paper after the visit; no emr fact is recorded for it here.
